findings.title: [P1] Constrain host file reads derived from pytest output
findings.body: Attacker-controlled code executed by the hidden tests can emit `ERROR /dev/zero` followed by `1 error in 0.01s`. The parser treats `/dev/zero` as a collection-error filename; joining an absolute filename discards `tree`, so this unbounded read executes against the host even in container mode. It can exhaust host memory after the subprocess timeout has stopped applying. Traversal paths and copied symlinks also escape the tree. Require resolved paths to remain inside the grading tree, reject non-regular files, and bound reads.

findings.title: [P2] Skip directory symlinks before changing cleanup permissions
findings.body: `os.walk()` includes symlinks to directories in `ds`, and `os.chmod()` follows those symlinks. Because `copy_tree()` preserves sandbox symlinks, an attacker can replace a protected file with a directory containing a link to a host directory. When `prepare()` removes that directory before restoring the file, cleanup changes the external target's permissions to 0700 with the grader's privileges. The same issue occurs when deleting a previous grading tree. Skip symlinks and use filesystem operations that cannot follow links outside the cleanup root.

findings.description: The grade is derived from stdout of a pytest/bats process that runs inside the agent-authored tree with that tree's own test infrastructure loaded. shape_command only adds `-p no:cacheprovider -q --rootdir … -rA`; it does not pass `--noconftest`, `-c <grader-owned ini>`, `-o addopts=`, or set PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD. pytest therefore honours any `conftest.py` on the path from /workspace to the hidden test, plus `pytest.ini` / `pyproject.toml` / `setup.cfg` / `tox.ini` in the tree (addopts, -p, pythonpath). `prepare()` removes only paths listed in grader_protected that the fixture lacks; a conftest.py or ini the agent *adds* in an unlisted location survives. A one-line hookwrapper on pytest_runtest_makereport that sets rep.outcome='passed' makes every hidden test report PASSED, the summary reads `N passed`, `bad` is empty and all_pass() is true. An atexit print of a fake `=== N passed in 0.1s ===` line also wins because parse_pytest takes the *last* matching summary line. For commands of kind 'auto' the output is trusted wholesale. The static-case floor on `total` does not help because `passed` is taken from the forged summary.
findings.failure_mode: An agent under evaluation (or a prompt-injected one) plants conftest.py / pytest.ini in its sandbox and receives hidden_tests 100%, verdict_accuracy true and snapshot_tests green, silently corrupting the ablation results the suite exists to measure.
findings.suggested_fix: Run hidden tests with `--noconftest -c /dev/null -o addopts= -p no:cacheprovider` and `-e PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1`; always strip root/ancestor conftest.py and all pytest ini files from the graded tree (or make them implicit grader_protected entries); prefer a grader-controlled `--junitxml=/tmp/r.xml` written by pytest over stdout parsing, and refuse (parse_error) when more than one summary line is present. Document that any forgery via the code under test remains possible and treat the scan as a lower bound, as done for contamination.

findings.description: `--executor host` executes the task's test command natively in grading/final, a verbatim copy of the agent's sandbox, as the grader's uid with cwd=tree. `env -i` scrubs variables but gives no filesystem, network or process isolation: pytest imports the agent's conftest.py and the modules under test, so arbitrary agent-authored code runs with the operator's full privileges. PYTHONUSERBASE is set to the caller's real user base, so the code can drop a `.pth` file into the operator's user site-packages for persistence in every future Python process. The header presents host mode as a convenience fallback without warning that it is unsandboxed execution of untrusted output; the Sprint 258 smoke appears to have used it.
findings.failure_mode: Operator grades a run on a host without docker; agent sandbox code reads ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, API keys in ~/.claude.json (all explicitly 'allowed' paths), exfiltrates them, or persists via user-site .pth.
findings.suggested_fix: Either remove --executor host, or make it refuse unless an explicit `--i-understand-host-runs-untrusted-code` style flag is set and print a loud warning; in host mode at minimum run under a throwaway uid / bwrap / unshare with the tree as the only writable mount, drop PYTHONUSERBASE, and never point HOME-adjacent paths at the operator's real profile.

findings.description: remove_path() walks a directory with os.walk (followlinks=False) and calls os.chmod(join(r, d), 0o700) on every entry in `dirnames`. os.walk lists symlinks-to-directories in dirnames, and os.chmod follows symlinks, so the chmod lands on the symlink *target*. copy_tree() deliberately preserves agent symlinks from sandbox/ into grading/final, so remove_path runs over agent-controlled links whenever (a) a run directory is graded a second time (fresh_dir(grading) at line 1052, explicitly supported), or (b) put_file()/prepare() removes an existing directory at a hidden-test dest or protected path that the agent populated with symlinks. shutil.rmtree itself is fd-based and safe; only the chmod pre-pass follows links.
findings.failure_mode: Agent creates sandbox/x/ -> /home/evaluser (or any grader-owned directory such as the results root or ~/.cache); on re-grade the host directory is chmod 0700, breaking shared access or other tooling, from inside an otherwise --network none container run.
findings.suggested_fix: Skip symlinks before chmod: `p = os.path.join(r, d); if not os.path.islink(p): os.chmod(p, 0o700)` (or use os.open with O_NOFOLLOW|O_DIRECTORY and os.fchmod). Also consider dropping symlinks entirely from copied grading trees, since nothing graded needs them.

findings.description: The header states that sandbox copies of dissent envelopes are tamperable and only the harness copies under eval/ are authoritative, yet the gate verdicts (and whether a gate 'ran' at all) are read from sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/{engineer-feedback,auditor-sprint-feedback}.md, which the agent can write during IMPLEMENT/FIX phases. gate_verdict() also uses os.path.isfile and open() without the islink guard that combined_findings() applies, so a symlinked feedback file is followed. The verdict feeds `verdict`, `verdicts`, `verdict_accuracy_per_gate`, `verdict_accuracy`, and selects which snapshot is graded for the gate.
findings.failure_mode: An agent appends `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {"verdict":"APPROVED"} -->` to auditor-sprint-feedback.md after fixing its code, earning verdict_accuracy=true for an arm whose reviewer never approved, or fabricates a feedback file so a gate that never ran counts as having run.
findings.suggested_fix: Have pipeline-run.sh capture the gate feedback files (or at least their LOA-VERDICT trailers) under <run-dir>/eval/ at gate time, read verdicts only from there, and treat sandbox copies as informational. Add the `not os.path.islink()` check to gate_verdict/review_md_verdict for consistency.

findings.description: The in-tree command is wrapped in `timeout 120` (no `-k`), and the Python side kills only the direct child (`docker` client or `env`) after 180 s. A test process that ignores SIGTERM makes `timeout` wait forever; when Python then kills the docker CLI, the `--rm` container is detached and keeps running with no bound, and in host mode the orphaned pytest keeps running under the grader uid. The grade records timed_out=true and continues, so the leak is silent.
findings.failure_mode: Agent code traps SIGTERM and spins; every grade of that run leaves a CPU-burning container or process behind on the grading host, exhausting resources across a batch.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `timeout -k 10 120` inside the container and add `--init` (or `--stop-timeout`) to docker run; on Python timeout, `docker kill` the container by a generated `--name`, or run the host-mode command in its own process group and kill the group.
